promptLatex: True or false: The claim 'every polynomial of even degree with real coefficients has a real root' is true. If false, provide a counterexample.
hintLatex: A real root means there is some real $x$ at which the polynomial evaluates to $0$.
For a polynomial to have a real root, its graph must reach the $x$-axis.
A polynomial of even degree with positive leading coefficient stays positive for large $|x|$.
solutionLatex: The claim is false. Consider $p(x) = x^4 + 1$. Its degree is $4$, which is even, and for every real $x$ we have $x^4 \ge 0$, so $p(x) = x^4 + 1 \ge 1 > 0$. The polynomial is therefore never $0$, and it has no real root. That single polynomial is the counterexample the claim needs.
